newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slack demand hits French wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: Slack demand hits French wheat prices.

text.p: French wheat slipped on Monday on slower demand for prompt delivery grain, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen for December delivery was quoted at 855 francs, down five on Friday.
Rouen wheat for January-March delivery was bid at 840 francs, down 10 francs on Friday.
French wheat firmed last week after the European Union increased the rebate on wheat exports to 16.59 Ecus tonne from 15.97 Ecus.
Dealers also said they were monitoring developments in a nationwide truck strike now in its eigth day, fearing it may disrupt grain supplies to port silos.
Barley prices ignored news Saudi Arabia was in the market to import 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley for January delivery.
Rouen barley for November-December delivery was offered at 840 francs, the level paid on Friday.
Wheat futures volume on MATIF reached a modest 100 lots in late afternoon, with February 1997 expiry quoted at 881 francs, up seven francs from Friday. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
